facts.statement: The species was first described as Titanosaurus colberti by Jain and Bandyopadhyay in 1997.
facts.quote: The type specimen of Isisaurus colberti, ISI R 335/1-65, was originally described and named as Titanosaurus colberti by Sohan Lal Jain and Saswati Bandyopadhyay in 1997.

facts.statement: Wilson and Upchurch established the genus Isisaurus in 2003.
facts.quote: In 2003, the fossils were designated as belonging to its own genus by Wilson and Upchurch.

facts.statement: The name Isisaurus honors the Indian Statistical Institute and means 'Indian lizard'.
facts.quote: The generic name, "Isisaurus," combines a reference to the Indian Statistical Institute (ISI) with the Greek "saurus," meaning "lizard."

facts.statement: Isisaurus possessed a short, upright neck and unusually long forelimbs compared to other sauropods.
facts.quote: It had a short, vertically directed neck and long forelimbs, making it considerably different from other sauropods.

facts.statement: The humerus bone of Isisaurus measures 148 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: The humerus is 148 centimetres long.

facts.statement: Isisaurus was a medium-sized sauropod estimated to reach 18 meters in length and weigh 15 metric tons.
facts.quote: Isisaurus was a medium-sized sauropod, with some estimates of its body length up to 18 m long and weighing 15 MT.

facts.statement: Isisaurus fossils have been found in the Late Cretaceous Lameta Formation of India and the Pab Formation of Pakistan.
facts.quote: Isisaurus (named after the Indian Statistical Institute) is a genus of titanosaurian dinosaur from the Late Cretaceous Lameta Formation of India and Pab Formation of Pakistan.

facts.statement: The holotype was discovered at Dongargaon Hill in the Maastrichtian Lameta Formation of India.
facts.quote: The site locality is Dongargaon Hill, which is in a Maastrichtian crevasse splay claystone in the Lameta Formation of India.

facts.statement: Isisaurus lived in central India and western Pakistan during the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Isisaurus lived in the area of present day central India and western Pakistan during the Maastrichtian age of the Cretaceous period.

facts.statement: Fossilized fungi found in coprolites attributed to Isisaurus suggest it ate leaves from various tree species.
facts.quote: Fungus in coprolites believed to have been voided by Isisaurus indicate that it ate leaves from several species of tree, since these fungi are known to be pathogens which infect tree leaves.

facts.statement: The exact classification of Isisaurus within the titanosaurian clade has been a subject of controversy.
facts.quote: While Isisaurus has consistently been considered to be a titanosaurian sauropod, its exact placement within this clade and its relationships with other titanosaurs has been controversial and problematic.

facts.statement: In 2021, Isisaurus was identified as the sister taxon to Arackar.
facts.quote: In 2021, Isisaurus was placed as the sister taxon to Arackar.

facts.statement: No skull, hindlimb, or foot bones have been found for Isisaurus.
facts.quote: No skull, hindlimb, or foot bones are known.

facts.statement: The original skeletal material discovered between 1984 and 1986 was found in an associated and mostly articulated condition.
facts.quote: The skeletal material found by Jain and Bandyopadhyay between 1984 and 1986 was "in associated and mostly articulated condition."

facts.statement: Isisaurus reached a length of 18 meters and a weight of 15 tons.
